(rule! (lambda (g)
      (let* ((gray (find-color g 5))
             (top (min-of fst gray)) (floor (max-of fst gray))
             (left (min-of snd gray)) (right (max-of snd gray))
             (rs (range top floor)) (cs (range (+ left 1) right))
             (row-empty? (lambda (r) (for/and ((c cs)) (zero? (at g r c)))))
             (n (/ (for/sum ((r rs)) (count-if (lambda (c) (zero? (at g r c))) cs)) (length cs))) (path (list (list 0 0) (list 0 1) (list 0 2) (list 1 2) (list 2 2) (list 2 1) (list 2 0) (list 1 0) (list 1 1))))
        (build-grid 3 3 (r c)
          (let ((idx (find-first (lambda (i) (and (= r (fst (nth path i)))
                                                 (= c (snd (nth path i))))) (range 9))))
            (if (and idx (< idx n)) 8 0))))))

intermediate: The strict interior bounds, per-row cyan occupancy, and the resulting set and count of wholly empty interior rows.
step_a: Find the gray U bounds, inspect cells strictly between its walls and above its floor, and count rows whose interior cells are all zero.
step_b: Use that count to select and paint the first min(count,9) positions of the episode-fixed clockwise or counterclockwise 3x3 cyan spiral.
why_b_depends_on_a: The row arrangement determines how many positions belong to the output prefix. Partial rows contain zeros without contributing an empty row, so replacing row classification by zero-area divided by width changes the selected prefix. Moving cyan into an empty row can change the output while preserving the color histogram.
